requirements.nl_text: Request Number - 7345 | Request Title - Better Media Saving Behavior | Request Description - I have:   searched open and closed issues for duplicates  read https://github.com/WhisperSystems/Signal-Android/wiki/Submitting-useful-bug-reports  Bug description. One of the features that was missing for a long time but thankfully has been recently implemented was the ability to swipe through the images without having to keep going back to the index and always having it start at the top. Kudos and thanks for that. However, another element exists that can be greatly improved and probably just got missed; and hopefully can be added. Currently each picture ("media") provides you the save button on the top. However, it never detects that the item has already been saved and you have to just remember it or go check your on device gallery to see if it is already there. Instead, it simply keeps making duplicates of the item and just incrementing it. It would't be too difficult to do a simple if/exists > show view/share icon else/doesn't > show save icon (as it is now). This will spare the need to save multiple duplicates and incrementing it when you can simply provide a visual check that it has already been saved. It is simply better UX and cleaner that way. Steps to reproduce.  save an item save it again you have a duplicate with a -1 at the end save it again you now have 3 with a -1 and -2 of the same item repeat and goes on as long as you keep saving Expected result: Detect that the item has already been saved and either provide a view icon or share icon to visually indicate it has been saved already, otherwise show the save button. A simple file system check for the item will facilitate this. Thanks in advance.
human_rimays: <MISSING_SCOPE>, if the "media item" has already been saved, then the App must change the "save icon" to a "view/share icon".
<MISSING_SCOPE>, if a picture has already been saved, then the App must show a view or share icon instead of the save button.
<MISSING_SCOPE>, if the user has already saved a "media item", then the App must show a "view" or "share" icon instead of the "save" button.
requirements.llm_rimay: For each picture, when the item has already been saved, the System shall detect that the item has already been saved based on a "file system check" and show a "view icon" or "share icon" instead of the save button.

verdict.text:
## Summary
Haiku zero-shot produces fluent Rimay that reaches about 90% of the human ceiling on embedding similarity. Its main weakness is fabrication. It filled 49 of 61 genuinely missing slots, nearly all of them scope and condition, and in several cases the invented content changes what the requirement means.

## Missing-slot detection
Track 1 is measurable here, because every slot has gold-missing support.

- **Scope and condition:** these are where the model fails. It flagged only 5 of 34 missing scopes and 3 of 21 missing conditions. Most of the hits come from one subset (5775-Signal, 1504-Signal, 42-Mastodon). Elsewhere it defaults to "For the system" and invents triggers.
- **Invented conditions with wrong content:** 7310-Signal adds "when a website maintainer adds a custom URL scheme". 937-Signal turns problem text into a condition and commits to one of three proposed ideas.
- **Action:** two missing actions were filled. 1504-Signal and 496-Signal received invented actions, although two of three annotators left 496's action missing.
- **Actor:** the model over-flags. It marked a present actor missing in 1363-Signal and an implied one missing in 592-Signal. In both cases it misplaced the placeholder, inserting `<MISSING_ACTOR>` inside the action phrase.
- **Requirement-level verdict:** 32 of 35 match the gold. This rests on only 4 gold-incomplete items, so one item moves F1 by roughly 0.15.

## Conversion quality
Relative to the human-human ceiling, the model is at roughly 90% on cosine, 77% on sequence ratio and 65% on Jaccard. The model therefore gets the meaning roughly right but diverges on surface form. Much of that gap is the fabricated scope and condition text, set against humans' uniform `<MISSING_SCOPE>, <MISSING_CONDITION>` prefix. 2943-Signal is a true semantic miss: the model asks for an explanation of why smileys were removed, while the annotators ask to restore them.

Paska passes 80% of outputs, but this flatters the model. Paska rewards well-formed slots and cannot see that they were invented. Several smells sit on fabricated material:
- Passive voice appears in the invented conditions of 937-Signal and 2055-Signal.
- Two atomic requirements were packed with multiple actions (6457-Signal, 7345-Signal).
- 83-Signal's "Not requirement" smell is correct, because every slot is gold-missing.

## Anomalies
- **Text outside the answer block** (316-Signal, 42-Mastodon, 5775-Signal, 6457-Signal, 6459-Signal, 7345-Signal): each case has 700–1000 characters of commentary.
  - Half of these fail Paska, against 4 of the other 29.
  - Paska segment IDs reach `rimay_3`/`rimay_4`, which suggests stray text may be reaching the smell detector. That would distort the Paska figures.
- **False non-atomic flag** (6077-Signal): an atomic requirement was flagged `<NON_ATOMIC>`. The slots still match apart from scope, so the headline metrics are barely affected.

## Next step
- Confirm that Paska and the slot parser read only the answer block, then re-score the six text-outside items.
- Add an explicit instruction that scope and condition are optional and must be `<MISSING_*>` unless the source states them. Then compare scope and condition flag rates for fsl and cot against this baseline.
- Report a fabrication-content audit separately from slot flags, starting with 7310-Signal, 937-Signal and 2943-Signal. Filled-versus-missing alone hides semantically wrong inventions.
